groups.subject: build(repo): pin toolchain, gate CI and document the conventions
groups.body:
Repository-level configuration for the target-generalization work.

- pyproject.toml: Python floor raised to 3.12 (the tree uses PEP 701 f-strings), ruff pinned to
  the 0.16 line with generated benchmark inputs excluded, new console scripts, and the
  pytest-timeout ceiling.
- CI (pr-fast.yml): the derive-don't-overfit gates, ledgers that may only shrink, local-path
  and holdout-name gates, and a docs freshness ratchet. Every build_tools check is either wired
  or listed with the reason it is not.
- .claude/ hooks refuse generated writes outside out/ and broad process kills on the shared
  host.
- CLAUDE.md states the conventions the gates enforce: derive target facts instead of hardcoding
  them, pin hardware revisions, one out/ root, one test suite, durable docs versus reports.

groups.subject: feat(tooling): add the repo gates and the measurement drivers
groups.body:
build_tools/scripts grows from a handful of helpers into the repository's enforcement and
measurement layer.

- Gates: target names, regex, assumed ISA constants, hardware provenance, fact provenance,
  holdout names and disjointness, artifact layout, docs freshness, local paths, module size,
  and a check that every *_ratchet.txt / *_allowlist.txt may only shrink. Each is fail-closed:
  a gate that cannot read its input reports that instead of passing.
- Generators: CLI, package, schema and docs-hub references, and a repository map derived from
  the tracked tree.
- Drivers for K1 board measurement, cross-framework baselines, FireSim/Zephyr legs, delivery
  bundles, and plots.

Everything is formatted with ruff 0.16.8.

groups.subject: feat(contract): capsule corpus, hardware pins and experiment ABI
groups.body:
The versioned, repository-independent contract that out-of-tree target backends are built and
graded against.

- capsules/: the generated and hand-authored capsule corpus for atlas, gemmini, mx_gemmini,
  radiance and saturn_opu -- ISA, layer, model-slice, whole-model and perf capsules -- with
  per-target profiles. Held-out capsules are counted, never named.
- hardware_pins.yaml: every external RTL, toolchain and simulator revision a verdict depends on,
  pinned by full sha and checked against the files actually read.
- rtl/, external/gsim/, perf_rules/: derived RTL facts, the GSIM engine build recipe, and cost
  rules.
- schemas/: target contract, command buffer, capsule and grading schemas.
- benchmarks/rvv_paper: the frozen study configuration for the RVV paper.

groups.subject: feat(common): shared paths, provenance, digests and storage
groups.body:
Library-wide helpers so each subsystem stops reimplementing them.

- paths: the out/ root and its runs/artifacts/build subtrees, .env-backed external checkouts.
- provenance: verify, record and require hardware pins; digest the bytes actually read.
- digest, jsonio, proc: one implementation each of sha256, canonical JSON hashing and checked
  subprocess execution.
- content_store and storage_cli (merlin-storage): hard-linked, content-addressed input closures,
  and a report and prune tool that reclaims only classes whose safety is a property.

groups.subject: feat(targetgen): derive targets from RTL and grade generated backends
groups.body:
TargetGen becomes target-agnostic: nothing it does is keyed on a target name.

- rtl/: extract structure and ISA facts from the target's own elaboration (CIRCT, FIRRTL census,
  decoder fan-out), with provenance on every fact and a registry that resolves where each
  target's RTL lives.
- The capsule runner, grading and tier promotion run a capsule cheapest-tier-first and keep the
  certificate bound to the digest of the bytes that earned it.
- sandbox/: the bwrap sandbox, frozen input closures, and answer-surface derivation for agent
  runs.
- rocc/, fixed_format/: decoders and assemblers for RoCC and self-hosted ISAs, derived from the
  target's facts.
- Conformance, capability discovery, affordability pricing per simulator engine, and ISA-versus-
  RTL cross-checking with an errata registry.

groups.subject: feat(targets): add muon, gemmini_universal, k1_cpu and voyager_accel
groups.body:
In-tree target definitions -- contracts, backends and tools -- consumed through the target
registry.

- muon: the SIMT backend for the radiance accelerator, with its Cyclotron engine binding.
- gemmini_universal: a sibling of gemmini (never an override) for the universal FPGA build.
- k1_cpu: the SpacemiT K1 CPU host target.
- voyager_accel: a draft descriptor for the Voyager accelerator.
- gemmini: the per-target backend, harness and tools moved out of shared library code.

groups.subject: feat(compile): whole-model lowering, block scheduling and RVV mining
groups.body:
The compiler plane from model capture to target binary.

- compile/: helpers split out of compile_cli (bundles, host lane, capacity, mesh execution) and
  a block scheduler driven by derived geometry.
- llvmlower/: linalg-to-LLVM whole-model lowering for rv64gcv and host, int8 and requant passes,
  and per-op profiling.
- kernels/, mining/: kernel mining and the RVV beam search that forks, builds and measures codegen
  packages on spike and the K1 board.
- xdsl_dialects/, frontends/, triton/: target-independent dialects, IR frontends, and a Triton
  kernel path to a command buffer.

groups.subject: feat(runtime): reference runtimes, substrate backends and liveness
groups.body:
Execution of command buffers and dispatch programs on each substrate.

- runtime/backends: spike, Zephyr on FireSim, and the K1 board backends (ours, OpenBLAS, XNNPACK),
  resolved through a backend registry rather than by name.
- Route partitioning: each command buffer identifies exactly one admission route.
- merlin/runtime: the bare-metal C runtime and its ABI.
- benchharness/, system/, liveness/: target-parametric benchmark primitives, system derivation,
  and a liveness oracle tier between functional and RTL.

groups.subject: feat(perf): a performance layer that prices what a target permits
groups.body:
What a target's legal choices cost, derived rather than assumed.

- perf/: archetypes and traits, a performance contract whose terms carry provenance and a validity
  domain, cycle and movement cost composition, FireSim receipts, and the phase-2 portfolio.
  perf/deps models the command-stream dependency graph.
- cost_model/ is removed; its roofline arithmetic now lives in perf.
- verify/: static (lit/FileCheck) and SMT verification of compiler passes.
- dse/, dse_guidance/, design_pressure/: the design-space pipeline, reworked on the shared helpers.

groups.subject: feat(baselines): frozen cross-framework comparisons and reports
groups.body:
External baselines and the comparison driver behind the published numbers.

- baselines/: ExecuTorch, TVM, buddy-mlir, exo, ggml and Voyager harnesses, with toolchains
  located from their contracts.
- compare/: a spec-driven comparison whose environment, packages and measurements are frozen and
  hashed, so a reported cell names the bytes it came from.
- plotting/, agentreport/: the house plotting style, and regenerable reports over agentic runs.

groups.subject: feat(experiments): unify the capsule bench and add the agent studies
groups.body:
The per-target capsule_bench_v0 directories (atlas, gemmini, mx_gemmini, radiance and
saturn_opu) are replaced by one capsule_bench driven by a per-target descriptor. Adding a target
is now a descriptor plus data, not a copied harness.

New experiments, each declaring its status in AGENT.md:
- agent_recipe_select_v0, cpu_host_compiler_v0, llm_kernel_vs_compiler_v0: agentic compiler
  studies.
- performance_contract, gsim_wholemodel: the performance layer's working register and whole-model
  GSIM runs.
- voyager_h2h, dataset_accuracy: the head-to-head against the Voyager compiler.
- agentic_report: regenerable reports over agent runs.

gemmini_perf_bench gains the phase-2 global performance experiment.

groups.subject: test(suite): one suite, organized by subsystem
groups.body:
All tests live in merlin/tests, in eight subsystem buckets (kernels, rvv, dse, gemmini,
targetgen, ir, runtime, infra), with shared inputs in fixtures/ and data/.

Tests whose subject is a particular target carry `pytest.mark.target(...)`, so
`pytest -m "not target"` runs the target-independent suite on its own.

The infra bucket carries regression tests for the gates themselves -- that each can fail,
that it refuses rather than passes when it cannot read its input, and that its ledger may
only shrink.

groups.subject: docs(hub): reference, guides and design notes with drift detection
groups.body:
docs/ is split into reference/, guides/ and design/. Each file carries front-matter
(owner, last_verified, code_refs), and a generated hub links them. A freshness gate reports any
doc whose code_refs changed after it was last verified.

examples/ adds end-to-end walkthroughs: a stock Triton kernel to an accelerator command buffer,
and the gemmelos and kodiak flows.

groups.subject: chore(out): track the output skeleton and curated reports only
groups.body:
Generated output lives under one out/ root: runs/, artifacts/ and build/. Only the skeleton
(AGENT.md, README) and curated reports the layout convention keeps are tracked. Raw run dumps
and vendored trees committed earlier are untracked here; they stay on disk and are ignored.
